frequency_question: How often do riparian states successfully renew or extend a bilateral water-sharing treaty before its expiration window closes, among comparable major treaty renewals?
membership_rule: Includes any bilateral interstate treaty governing shared transboundary river flows that has a fixed multi-decade duration and comes up for formal renewal or renegotiation. Excludes multilateral basins without specific bilateral allocation treaties, and treaties without fixed expiration dates.
window: Within the final 24 months leading up to and including the expiration date of the predecessor treaty.

cases.name: U.S.-Mexico 1944 Water Treaty Amendments (Minute 319 and Minute 323 successors)
Columbia River Treaty (Canada-USA) regime adjustments and renewal talks window
India-Pakistan Indus Waters Treaty periodic commission renewals / extensions
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II operational extensions

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named; represents the primary modern instances of multi-decade transboundary water treaties reaching formal renewal milestones.
known_gaps: Limited global set of multi-decade bilateral water treaties reaching exact expiration windows in contemporary history.
skeleton: 4 major bilateral water treaty renewal instances reviewed across international river basins
validity_reason: Bilateral water diplomacy frameworks evolve slowly over decades, so historical compliance and renewal patterns remain stable over a multi-year horizon.
